candidates.label: Judea (historical region)
candidates.support: Wikidata's item for the historical region of Judea gives a representative point in the Judean hill country; as a broad region rather than a single site, any point is only an approximate reference, cross-checked against OpenBible.info's separate identification of the same region name.

summary.text: Judea was the southern part of the historical land of Israel in the first century AD, encompassing Jerusalem and the surrounding hill country, and gave its name to the Herodian and Roman administrative units that governed the area through the New Testament period.

history.text: After Herod the Great's death in 4 BC, Judea proper passed to his son Herod Archelaus as ethnarch; when Rome deposed Archelaus in AD 6, Judea became a Roman province administered first by a prefect and later by a procurator, normally based at Caesarea Maritima.
